facts.statement: Sinohelicoprion is an extinct genus of eugeneodontid fish known as the "Chinese spiral saw".
facts.quote: Sinohelicoprion (meaning "Chinese spiral saw" or "Chinese Helicoprion") is an extinct genus of eugeneodontid fish

facts.statement: H. T. Liu and M. N. Chang first named and classified the genus in 1963.
facts.quote: It was first named and classified by H. T. Liu and M. N. Chang in 1963.

facts.statement: The genus belongs to the parent group Helicampodontidae.
Sinohelicoprion is classified within the family Helicampodontidae.
The animal is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
Fossil evidence places the animal's time range strictly within the Changhsingian stage, from 254.14 to 251.902 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Changhsingian to Changhsingian (254.14 to 251.902 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The animal lived from 254 to 251 million years ago, spanning the late Permian and possibly the Early Triassic.
rejected.quote: It lived during the late Permian and possibly the Early Triassic, from 254 to 251 million years ago.
